eyebrow: Checking one resource group for a tag
code:
ENV_TAG=$(az group show --name "$RG" \
  --query "tags.Environment" -o tsv)

if [ -z "$ENV_TAG" ]; then
  echo "MISSING: $RG has no Environment tag"
else
  echo "OK: $RG -> Environment=$ENV_TAG"
fi
caption: An empty query result means no tag — [ -z ] catches it the same way it catches any empty variable.

code:
#!/bin/bash
RESOURCE_GROUPS=$(az group list --query "[].name" -o tsv)

for RG in $RESOURCE_GROUPS; do
  ENV_TAG=$(az group show --name "$RG" \
    --query "tags.Environment" -o tsv)
  if [ -z "$ENV_TAG" ]; then
    echo "MISSING: $RG has no Environment tag"
  else
    echo "OK: $RG -> Environment=$ENV_TAG"
  fi
done
caption: chmod +x check-tags.sh, then ./check-tags.sh reports every group in one pass.
